artifacts.summary: Re-derives the nine ci.yml checks' exact invocations, order, exit-code conventions, lock/sequencing behavior, and documentation-placement precedent for scripts/verify-all.sh, CONTRIBUTING.md, and scripts/README.md.

memory_candidates.content: BimodalLogic's ci.yml nine-check gate has argument drift from a plausible bare-name reading: check-copyright-headers.sh and readme-lint.sh are both invoked with 'FormalSystem BimodalTools' (not bare --strict / no args) because both scripts default to ROOTS=("FormalSystem") only; 'lake exe mk_all' is invoked as '--lib FormalSystem --check' (bare '--check' errors on the two Tests-rooted libraries). Also, the 'lint-style' CI step is actually three sub-checks under one outcome: lake exe lint-style, an executable-bit scan over tracked .lean files, and a case-insensitive tracked-path collision scan.

BimodalLogic's scripts/README.md documents a 'Per-script determinations' table classifying each gate script's use of the shared .lake/build-guard.lock (flock-based, advisory, leaf-only: only the script that invokes lake/lean takes it, never a delegating caller). A sequential caller script that invokes several lock-taking child scripts one after another has no deadlock risk, since each child acquires and releases the lock before the next starts -- only parallel/backgrounded invocation of lock-taking scripts would be hazardous.

BimodalLogic's docs/development/CI_CD_PROCESS.md 'Wiring a New Check Script' section (around line 214) is the canonical convention for adding a ci.yml check step: step naming mirrors exact invocation, every check is continue-on-error:true with the final 'Report results' step as the sole aggregating gate (expected count + report() per step), a skip-and-report-neutral convention for legitimately-absent inputs (print 'SKIP (neutral): <reason>' and exit 0, as check-paper-definitions.sh does), and cache-warm placement (lake-dependent checks after the build steps). Useful precedent for any local aggregator mirroring CI's reporting shape.
